title: `first`, `last`, `any_value`, `mode`, `min_by`/`max_by` take a row that depends on the partitioning
verdict: `tie_pick`: input order within a partition, partitions in completion order; `mode` any of the tie
description: `first(x)` and `last(x)` take the first and last row in the order the rows reach the aggregate, NULL included unless `ignoreNulls` is true (`first(x, true)`). Over one partition that is input order; after a shuffle it is the order of the partitions' rows, which Spark documents as non-deterministic (over a 3-partition `range(0, 1000)` they gave 279 and 635). `min_by(v, k)` and `max_by(v, k)` take the row with the least or greatest `k`, among ties the last one seen in the probes (`b` and `d`); they skip NULL keys.
`mode(x)` returns one of the most frequent values, any of a tie (`maxBy` over a hash map); `mode(x, true)` the lowest; `mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC)` the highest. NULLs are skipped.

`collect_list`, `array_agg`, `string_agg` and `listagg` keep the order the rows arrive in, NULLs skipped (3, 1, 2 in input order; a different order after a shuffle); `listagg(...) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...)` sorts. `collect_set` has no stated order.
reference: `tie_pick`: any row of the group (each measure may take its own); `tie_order`: any order for `string_agg` and `array_agg`. Every Spark choice is allowed.

evidence.note: `eval`: `maxBy(_._2)` over the counts, or by `(count, key)` when ordered
the docs: any of the tied values unless `deterministic`

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `collect_list` and `array_agg` of (1), (2), (1) give [1,2,1], the input order of one VALUES partition
`listagg(col2)` without WITHIN GROUP: the test checks only lengths and letter counts, not order; NULLs skipped, a group of NULLs gives NULL
`listagg(col1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col2)` sorts: aabb
`mode(salary)` over 17 distinct salaries returns 10563, one of the tie
`mode(col, true)` over -10, 0, 10 returns the lowest, -10 (`mode(col)` gives 0)
`mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary)` gives the lowest of the tie, 5186, and `ORDER BY salary DESC` the highest, 11798

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
